","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

Commands (use /deepducking; /dduck is an alias):
/deepducking [toggle main window]
/dduck [alias for /deepducking; accepts all commands below]
/deepducking mini [toggle Mini]
/deepducking settings [open Settings]
/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]
/deepducking party-start [floor] [alias for start]
/deepducking party [select fixed-party POTD while idle]
/deepducking adopt [bind eligible already-entered party dungeon]
/deepducking hold [pause local output; retain run for Resume]
/deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]
/deepducking saves info <dungeon> [inspect native saves]
/deepducking saves delete <dungeon> <1|2> [delete selected save after native checks; no extra confirmation]
/deepducking saves dof <dungeon> <1|2> <on|off> [set future-failure deletion preference; no deletion now]
/deepducking saves cancel [cancel pending save or Start preparation; completed actions remain]

Dungeon arguments: potd, hoh, eo, pt. [floor] is optional; <...> is required. Choose one value for 1|2 or on|off; omit brackets when typing. Start can replace stopped state; Resume can release an eligible retained in-dungeon run. nextstop and ns retain the save and keep Mini open until return is observed; repeat to confirm the same request. Use the existing boss-break button to cancel.

If DailyDuty is installed, /dd is unavailable for Deep Ducking; use /deepducking. An alias owned by another plugin is preserved.

- Hunting Log. Jobs has a Hunting Log frame. It shows each class's rank, its tasks complete, and the monsters it still needs, with the place. Import a Tales of Milestones export to fill it in.
- Gear guide. Jobs has a Gear guide frame. Select one job and level. It shows the highest item level for each slot from the sources that you tick, with options for your export, crafting, NPC vendors and the market board.
- Mentor Roulette readiness. The Mentor tab has a Roulette frame, also listed under Jobs and Duties. It shows the Battle Mentor requirements: the level 100 role quests, a combat job at level 100, and each duty in the game's Mentor Roulette pool cleared once. Missing duties are listed by expansion and type. Item level 755 is a manual check, because the export does not have it.

- Allied societies. When every society in a group is at its last rank and the Intersocietal Quests are done, the group shows only the names, ranks and the quest check box.
- Fix: Ocean Fishing clock. The bar shows the time as "29:58" again, not "00:29:58".
- Fix: new characters. A new character no longer stops the Quest items frame after you enter a crafter or gatherer level. "Mark items HQ" is on by default again.
- Fix: backup import. A backup with no characters no longer leaves the page empty until a reload.
- Fix: Challenge Log. The Challenge Log list now comes from the game's data, so it matches the game after a patch.
- Fix: smaller items. The Collections filter (All, Owned, Missing) keeps its selection when you change area. Collapsed sections stay collapsed. Ended events leave the events feed. The time zone and hunt switches work with Space and Enter.

    * Some more changes coming soon but emergency maintenance started RIP

    * Reawakened Fangs Feature now also applies to Steel Maw.
    
    1.5.0.79:

    * Meisui/Tenri priority fixed and DWaD to Meisui added.
    * Monk's Draconic Leap feature now properly syncs below level 50 when you don't have a form.
    * Raise Hard Target Lockout Feature added.
    
    1.5.0.72:
    * Double Down features now account for its new cost.
    * New option for Royal Authority to Atonement where it will only activate if you are about to overwrite Sword Oath in your combo.
    * Empyreal Arrow will no longer turn into Pitch Perfect under any circumstances.
    
    1.5.0.71:
    * Updated for 7.1 compatibility.

    * Added an 'Only When Full' option to Sidewinder to Pitch Perfect.

    1.5.0.70:
    * Added Comet Overwrite Prevention feature. Or did I?
    * Removed Holy overcap features (it made no sense when you gain, not lose, DPS by letting it overcap).
    
    1.5.0.69 (Nice):
    * Sacrificium Feature added.
    * Despair to Flare Star added.
    * Dragon Kick to Forbidden Chakra added.
    
    1.5.0.67:
    * Blizzard 3 & 2 to Flare Star feature added.
    
    1.5.0.61:
    * Lucid Dreaming Reminders now have a configurable MP threshold, as well as a configurable cooldown remaining offset where they stop replacing the cooldown.
    
    1.5.0.60:
    * Combos to Saber Dance during Devilment feature added.
    * Some other stuff added to Dancer, too. Maybe.
    * Phlegma to Psyche added.
    
    1.5.0.59:
    * Isle Sprint feature added.
    
    1.5.0.53:
    * Reaving Steel added from regular XIVComboExpanded. Maybe something else, too? Tis a secret.
    * Hooking Hooksets and Chummy Cast added.
    
    1.5.0.51:
    * Chaotic Glide added.
    
    1.5.0.49:
    * Standard Step into Technical Step added.
    
    1.5.0.41:
    * Viper features added. {"Author":"Legends of the Game","Name":"Tales of Milestones","InternalName":"TimeMemoriaV3","AssemblyVersion":"3.16.0.15","Description":"Quest progression and pacing — a reflective notebook for your story journey, not a scoreboard.","ApplicableVersion":"any","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3","Tags":["quest","quests","progression","pacing"],"CategoryTags":["utility"],"DalamudApiLevel":15,"LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"CanUnloadAsync":false,"LoadPriority":0,"Punchline":"Remember every step, Warriors of Light.","AcceptsFeedback":true,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/releases/latest/download/latest.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/releases/latest/download/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/releases/latest/download/latest.zip","IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/main/assets/icon.png","DownloadCount":0,"Changelog":"Tales of Milestones:
- Hunting Log window (`/hunt`). A new optional feature. Type `/hunt`, or switch it on in Settings. The window shows every Hunting Log monster that you still need, for all your unlocked classes and your Grand Company at the same time. You do not have to change class to see a class's log. Each row shows the class, the task, the monster, your kills and where to find it. Finished monsters, finished ranks and locked classes are not shown.
- Map flags for Hunting Log monsters. Click Flag on a row to open the map at that monster. If the monster is also in your current zone, the row shows that location. The locations come from the Hunty plugin by Infiziert90 (MIT License).
- Current class only and Current zone only. Two check boxes in the Hunting Log window. With Current zone only, the window shows only the monsters in the zone where you are, for all classes. The window updates when you change class or zone.
- Change class from the Hunting Log. In the summary line at the top of the window, click a class name to equip a gear set for that class. If you have more than one gear set for the class, a list opens and you select one. The game's own Gear Set function does the change, the same as a click in the Gear Set window. Nothing is sent to chat.
- Hunting Log in the export. The export has a new `huntLog` block with each class's rank and kill counts. The Adventurer's Ledger reads it.
- Leve markers. In the quest list, a leve whose items are in your bags now shows "[R]" in place of a check mark. The check mark means "complete" in the News panel. Hold the pointer on a leve row to see what "> " and "[R]" mean.
- Fix: allied societies in the mini window. The society list shows only societies that are capped and wait for a main quest. Societies at their last rank are not listed.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Hunting Log. Jobs has a Hunting Log frame. It shows each class's rank, its tasks complete, and the monsters it still needs, with the place. Import a Tales of Milestones export to fill it in.
- Gear guide. Jobs has a Gear guide frame. Select one job and level. It shows the highest item level for each slot from the sources that you tick, with options for your export, crafting, NPC vendors and the market board.
- Mentor Roulette readiness. The Mentor tab has a Roulette frame, also listed under Jobs and Duties. It shows the Battle Mentor requirements: the level 100 role quests, a combat job at level 100, and each duty in the game's Mentor Roulette pool cleared once. Missing duties are listed by expansion and type. Item level 755 is a manual check, because the export does not have it.
- Import preview: Challenge Log. When an export opens new Challenge Log entries, the import preview shows them, for example "Challenge Log entries open: 40 → 41 (new: Soul Survivor I)".
- Allied societies. When every society in a group is at its last rank and the Intersocietal Quests are done, the group shows only the names, ranks and the quest check box.
- Fix: Ocean Fishing clock. The bar shows the time as "29:58" again, not "00:29:58".
- Fix: new characters. A new character no longer stops the Quest items frame after you enter a crafter or gatherer level. "Mark items HQ" is on by default again.
- Fix: backup import. A backup with no characters no longer leaves the page empty until a reload.
- Fix: Challenge Log. The Challenge Log list now comes from the game's data, so it matches the game after a patch.
- Fix: smaller items. The Collections filter (All, Owned, Missing) keeps its selection when you change area. Collapsed sections stay collapsed. Ended events leave the events feed. The time zone and hunt switches work with Space and Enter.
- Faster pages. The Ledger draws only the area and frame on screen.","SourceRepo":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/main/repo.json"}

{"Author":"Legends of the Game","Name":"Tales of Milestones","InternalName":"TimeMemoriaV3","AssemblyVersion":"3.16.0.15","Description":"Quest progression and pacing — a reflective notebook for your story journey, not a scoreboard.","ApplicableVersion":"any","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3","Tags":["quest","quests","progression","pacing"],"CategoryTags":["utility"],"DalamudApiLevel":15,"LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"CanUnloadAsync":false,"LoadPriority":0,"Punchline":"Remember every step, Warriors of Light.","AcceptsFeedback":true,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/releases/latest/download/latest.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/releases/latest/download/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/releases/latest/download/latest.zip","IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/main/assets/icon.png","DownloadCount":0,"Changelog":"Tales of Milestones:
- Hunting Log window (`/hunt`). A new optional feature. Type `/hunt`, or switch it on in Settings. The window shows every Hunting Log monster that you still need, for all your unlocked classes and your Grand Company at the same time. You do not have to change class to see a class's log. Each row shows the class, the task, the monster, your kills and where to find it. Finished monsters, finished ranks and locked classes are not shown.
- Map flags for Hunting Log monsters. Click Flag on a row to open the map at that monster. If the monster is also in your current zone, the row shows that location. The locations come from the Hunty plugin by Infiziert90 (MIT License).
- Current class only and Current zone only. Two check boxes in the Hunting Log window. With Current zone only, the window shows only the monsters in the zone where you are, for all classes. The window updates when you change class or zone.
- Change class from the Hunting Log. In the summary line at the top of the window, click a class name to equip a gear set for that class. If you have more than one gear set for the class, a list opens and you select one. The game's own Gear Set function does the change, the same as a click in the Gear Set window. Nothing is sent to chat.
- Hunting Log in the export. The export has a new `huntLog` block with each class's rank and kill counts. The Adventurer's Ledger reads it.
- Leve markers. In the quest list, a leve whose items are in your bags now shows "[R]" in place of a check mark. The check mark means "complete" in the News panel. Hold the pointer on a leve row to see what "> " and "[R]" mean.
- Fix: allied societies in the mini window. The society list shows only societies that are capped and wait for a main quest. Societies at their last rank are not listed.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Hunting Log. Jobs has a Hunting Log frame. It shows each class's rank, its tasks complete, and the monsters it still needs, with the place. Import a Tales of Milestones export to fill it in.
- Gear guide. Jobs has a Gear guide frame. Select one job and level. It shows the highest item level for each slot from the sources that you tick, with options for your export, crafting, NPC vendors and the market board.
- Mentor Roulette readiness. The Mentor tab has a Roulette frame, also listed under Jobs and Duties. It shows the Battle Mentor requirements: the level 100 role quests, a combat job at level 100, and each duty in the game's Mentor Roulette pool cleared once. Missing duties are listed by expansion and type. Item level 755 is a manual check, because the export does not have it.
- Import preview: Challenge Log. When an export opens new Challenge Log entries, the import preview shows them, for example "Challenge Log entries open: 40 → 41 (new: Soul Survivor I)".
- Allied societies. When every society in a group is at its last rank and the Intersocietal Quests are done, the group shows only the names, ranks and the quest check box.
- Fix: Ocean Fishing clock. The bar shows the time as "29:58" again, not "00:29:58".
- Fix: new characters. A new character no longer stops the Quest items frame after you enter a crafter or gatherer level. "Mark items HQ" is on by default again.
- Fix: backup import. A backup with no characters no longer leaves the page empty until a reload.
- Fix: Challenge Log. The Challenge Log list now comes from the game's data, so it matches the game after a patch.
- Fix: smaller items. The Collections filter (All, Owned, Missing) keeps its selection when you change area. Collapsed sections stay collapsed. Ended events leave the events feed. The time zone and hunt switches work with Space and Enter.
- Faster pages. The Ledger draws only the area and frame on screen.","_SourceId":"legendsofthegame-timememoriav3","_SourceName":"LegendsOfTheGame / TimeMemoriaV3","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/main/repo.json","_Category":"automation"}

{"Author":"The Combat Reborn Team","Name":"Rotation Solver Reborn","InternalName":"RotationSolver","Description":"Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.

This means almost all the information available in one frame in combat, including the status of all players in the party, the status of any hostile targets, skill cooldowns, the MP and HP of characters, the location of characters, casting status of the hostile target, combo, combat duration, player level, etc.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.340","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v1.0.4.343 (2026-11-25) [testing]
- **NIN: Fuma Shuriken is no longer suggested while Ten is not ready.** The mudra helper could offer Fuma Shuriken when the Ten action itself was still on cooldown, spending the mudra window on a suggestion that would not fire; the placement now checks the action is ready first (upstream WrathCombo fix).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.342 (2026-11-24) [testing]
- **The Beastmaster Crucible rules now treat the first master board's ice dragon fight as a knockback fight.** The dive's push (about thirty yalms) resolves on a one-second cast with a half-second fallback bar, and both bars are now in the knockback table, so Vileskin is held for the push there instead of being spent on ordinary target picks - the same policy the other sixteen knockback fights already follow, from the same upstream fight-module source. The fight has not been played on this install, so the timing comes from those modules rather than recorded runs.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.341 (2026-11-17) [testing]
- **The Fight Brain countdown strip no longer keeps past forecasts on screen.** A clock mix-up inside the forecast tick compared the entries' Unix timestamps against the machine's uptime clock, so the rule that drops a forecast three seconds after its moment passed could never fire: old entries piled up, filled the forecast list, and the strip showed a fixed set of entries whose countdowns grew ever more negative for the rest of the session. The tick now prunes on the same clock the entries carry, and the strip itself shows only entries still ahead (with one second of grace), so a fight's leftovers disappear instead of counting up in the negative.
- **The Fight Brain countdown strip only draws during combat now.** Outside a fight it draws nothing, even while the forecast source is still answering, so the strip no longer sits on the screen between fights.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.340 (2026-11-15) [testing]
- The settings window has been rebuilt in the same custom window style as the other plugins and polished for the real in-game font and scale, with every preset, option and saved setting unchanged.
- The window uses a two-level layout: Combos, Automation and System tabs, a row of destinations for the open tab, a page header and a status footer that stays in view. Long pages fade out above the footer instead of being cut off.
- Preset cards have even padding, a larger title and toggles that sit inside the card, and a whole toggle row, label included, can be clicked. Search keeps one width on every page, shows a dimmed hint, has a clear button and reports a result count.
- The problem report button sits in the footer so it is reachable on every page and window size, and the status pill shows a running rotation in green and a blocked one in amber.
- This build also picks up the restyled shared What's new window and Report a problem popup.

v1.0.4.339 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyCrafter","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.7.13","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.1.7.15 (2026-11-21) [testing]
- Crafts that were waiting on a material WahTools handed back no longer run into a wall of failed-craft lines in the same pass. They are pulled out of the wave's craft queue the moment the hand-back happens, their rows on the Run tab show them waiting for the next pass, and the re-plan remakes them on the material's new route.
- Crafts no longer start while WahTools Hunter is still driving the character after a hunt. The hand-off to Artisan now waits for WahTools to go idle, the same gate the other WahTools hand-offs use, and logs one line when it does.
- The blocked report now lists the fish and monster-drop materials WahTools was handed, so the Run tab and /lcraft status show what a blocked run is waiting on.
- WahTools' Hunter is now offered an item's monsters in a smarter order: the highest-level monster the character can already beat first, then monsters with no known level, then monsters above the character's combat level from the lowest up. The level data comes from the installed WahTools itself; when it cannot be read, a warning is logged once per session and the previous order is kept.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.7.14 (2026-11-21) [testing]
- **Monster-drop materials can be hunted with WahTools.** When WahTools is loaded, a material that a known monster drops is handed to WahTools' Hunter instead of going straight to the market-board list. Hunter counts kills, not drops, so the run hunts in batches, recounts the bags between batches, and stops as soon as enough have landed. It gives up after two batches in a row that drop nothing (or eight in total), and the rest goes back on the market-board or manual list on the next pass. Gil-vendor items, and currency-shop items the character can already pay for, are still bought, never hunted.
- **Fish materials can be caught with WahTools.** When WahTools is loaded, a fish that no gathering node yields goes to WahTools' Feesh instead of GatherBuddyReborn. A fish WahTools will not take, such as an ocean fish, goes back to GatherBuddyReborn on the next pass. The caught fish stay protected from WahTools' own discard and desynth rules until the run ends, including while a blocked run waits for Resume.
- Both run after GatherBuddyReborn and before Artisan, and crafts that need them wait for them. Each has its own setting under Dispatch behavior, both on by default; with WahTools absent or both settings off, routing is exactly as before. Stop ends a WahTools fish or hunt in progress.
- The Integrations list shows whether WahTools is loaded.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.7.13 (2026-11-15) [testing]
- The window was polished for the real in-game font and scale: text no longer clips or sits against card borders.
- The catalog table keeps its sortable, resizable and reorderable columns and its right-click menu for showing and hiding columns; columns that do not fit start hidden.
- Numeric column headers line up with the figures beneath them in the catalog, cart, ledger and run tables, and no header is cut mid-word at larger UI scales.
- Recipe details are organised into summary, ingredient and market cards, with source and unit price under each ingredient and the fulfil buttons beside them.
- The Settings and Run pages no longer repeat the same warning or state word, and short windows get a compact page header that leaves more room for the table.

v0.1.7.12 (2026-11-15) [testing]
- The plugin window now uses a responsive card-based shell for catalog, cart, run and settings, with integrated area navigation, destination search, live page counts, a close button in the header and persistent dispatch and footer actions. Catalog logic, cart editing, dispatch, integrations and saved configuration are unchanged.

v0.1.7.11 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

{"Author":"The Combat Reborn Team","Name":"Rotation Solver Reborn","InternalName":"RotationSolver","Description":"Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.

{"Author":"GitHixy","Name":"HitSpark","Punchline":"Replace the game's combat numbers with animated, styleable fly text.","Description":"HitSpark replaces Final Fantasy XIV's combat text with its own renderer: better fonts, tuned motion and real impact on critical hits.

WHAT YOU GET

- Every kind of combat text redrawn: damage dealt and taken, healing, misses and evades, status effects, experience, crafting and loot.
- Eight built-in presets, each a complete look: Classic+, Heroic, Tally, Onslaught, Elemental, Grim, Minimal and Retro.
- Real motion: arcs, fountains, rising and falling paths, scrolling columns, and punch, shake, flash, sparks and trails on crits.
- Multi-hits and damage over time that roll up into one number, with DoT ticks in their own colour.
- Other players' numbers shown smaller, or hidden, for your party and for everyone else, with a distance limit.
- Rear and flank hints for positionals, and an option to let numbers pass under the game's UI.

- Read achievement counts. This button replaces "Read hunt counts" on the Progression tab, in both windows. It asks the game for 19 counts, one at a time (about 12 seconds): gathered collectables, crafted collectables, duties, and the 16 A and S rank hunt groups. You do not have to open the Achievements window first. It runs only when you press it.
- Read counts, copy everything. A new button. It reads the same 19 counts, then copies the full export when the read ends. This button and "Read achievement counts" send the only requests that the plugin sends to the game server.

- Smaller hunt groups in the export. The export no longer repeats each hunt group's name. The Adventurer's Ledger uses the id.
- Fix: old collectable and duty counts. A newer reading of an earlier tier could be ignored in favour of an older reading of a later tier, so a count could stay too low. The higher count now stays, whatever tier it came from.
- Fix: reading times. After a plugin reload, the last achievement read is no longer given a new time.
- Fix: long food names. In `/tm food`, a long name no longer covers the text on its right.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Relic grids. The relic grids show each row in its tier colour, as the stage bar does. The Cosmic and Eureka grids count every stage (220 and 240).
- Fix: relic cards. A relic card that has a starting quest no longer says "no starting quest".
- Fix: job tables. The "not levelled" note counts only the jobs in its own table and shows only in that table's frame."}

engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

the plugin does:

  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes

name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link
trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

  world character typed as text

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"PvP Solver","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.2.18","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v0.1.2.36 (2026-11-25)
- Basic/Actions/ActionTargetInfo.cs FindTargetAreaFriend: ground-targeted beneficial placement now snaps to the terrain and is kept inside the action's range and the player's line of sight before it is used (upstream RotationSolverReborn 'Fix for ground targeting actions', ported onto the fork's carried ground-target subsystem). Spots the old code took at face value - saved beneficial positions, the tank's position, the point between the player and the attacked party member - can no longer land behind a wall or under the floor.
- After the server rejects a ground-targeted action, the ground-target finder targets the player's own position for five seconds before trying the placement again. The rejection is read from the existing ActorControl hook (ActionTimeline/ActionTimelineManager.cs, category 0x2BC, second argument 1) and recorded in DataCenter (Basic/DataCenter.cs _actionRejectedTicks), matching upstream's Watcher feed.
- The tank and saved-spot steps of the ground-target finder were restructured into upstream's helper shape (FindTargetAreaTank with a two-pass stance scan and an effect-range check, FindBeneficialPosition with a flat-distance gate, TryGetGroundPosition with a 0.5-range margin); the boss-position step and the arena-center fallback upstream added are NOT ported - the fork removed them as PvE remnants in v0.1.2.30. The 'Use beneficial ground-targeted actions' setting's description (Basic/Configuration/Configs.cs) now describes the fork's actual fallback order.
- UI/RotationConfigWindow.cs: the 'Add position' button places the saved spot through the same terrain-snap helper (ObjectHelper.SnapToGround) instead of its own inline raycast, and Basic/Helpers/ObjectHelper.cs extracts that raycast into one shared Raycast helper that also serves line-of-sight checks.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.35 (2026-11-22)
- Basic/Helpers/StatusHelper.cs LocksActions: action-locking statuses are now detected reliably - Out of the Action (statuses 1113, 1284 and 1462) counts as locking actions even when the game data sheet does not flag it, and a status with no remaining time counts as still active instead of expiring instantly. Rotation updates now pause correctly through those lockout states (read by Updaters/ActionUpdater.cs).
- Basic/Actions/ActionTargetInfo.cs FindTarget and GetCanTargets, and Basic/Actions/BaseAction.cs and IBaseAction.cs CanUse, accept an optional extra target filter passed by the caller; no built-in PvP action passes one yet, so target selection behaves exactly as before. This keeps the engine aligned with upstream RotationSolverReborn for future fixes.
- Basic/Rotations/CustomRotation_BasicInfo.cs adds a ShouldDelayCommandAction hook, checked by the commanded-action paths in CustomRotation_Ability.cs and CustomRotation_GCD.cs before firing a commanded action immediately; the default answer is no, so commanded actions fire exactly as before.

v0.1.2.34 (2026-11-21)
- Basic/Rotations/CustomRotation_GCD.cs GCD: the chooser never called the job rotations' GeneralGCD, so no attack GCD was ever selected - the character could only auto-heal, Guard, Recuperate and drink the elixir, which read as healing instead of attacking in matches. The call was deleted together with the duty-rotation engine in v0.1.2.23 (the same class of loss as the v0.1.2.32 rotation-load fix), so every version from v0.1.2.23 to v0.1.2.33 shipped with attack GCDs as dead code. GeneralGCD is called again inside the NoCasting branch, in upstream's chooser order (heals first, attacks after).
- Basic/Rotations/CustomRotation_GCD.cs GCD: the DefenseArea and DefenseSingle branches were emptied by the same removal, so the healer PvP rotations' defense GCD overrides were equally unreachable; both calls are restored. No duty-rotation, Provoke or other PvE machinery returns.
- Commands/RSCommands_Actions.cs DoAction: every executed-action change now leaves one "ActionTap: <name> (<id>)" log line (on-change only, so it cannot spam). This makes the live-path release check possible: a real match must show attack actions being chosen before any build is called good.
- tests/PvPSolver.RotationHarness Cases/SelectionGate.cs: the release harness now fails when the compiled chooser no longer calls GeneralGCD (IL call-site count and position after the heal branch), when the ability chooser loses GeneralAbility, when any shipped PvP rotation loses its attack-bearing GeneralGCD override, or when the ActionTap log line is missing from the built assembly.

v0.1.2.33 (2026-11-21)
- Commands/RSCommands_Actions.cs UpdateRotationState: "Turn on when a match starts" could never engage - it only ran during the match loading screen, when no player object exists and the job role is unknown, so the null-player early return and the job-role check silently dropped it and the rotation loaded but never acted in matches. The auto-on now latches during the load screen (new pure decision core Basic/Decisions/MatchStartAutoOn.cs) and engages the PvP state on the first cycle where the player and job are loaded, logging both steps.
- RotationSolverPlugin.cs constructor and Commands/RSCommands_BasicInfo.cs RSCommands.Enable: the /pvpsolver, /pvs, "/pvpsolver Auto" and "/pvpsolver Off" handlers were registered only near the end of a 10-30 second start-up (after nine windows, the icon cache and the status lists), so commands typed while the plugin was still starting read as "Command not found". Registration now runs first, right after the configuration loads, and a start-up log line lists every command and its registration result.
- Commands/RSCommands_StateSpecialCommand.cs UpdateState and DoOneCommandType: rotation state changes and ignored role-less commands are logged, so a state that silently never engages can no longer hide behind a clean log.
- tests/PvPSolver.RotationHarness Cases/MatchStartAutoOnCases.cs and Cases/CommandGate.cs: the release harness now fails the build when a documented slash command has no registration call site in the built assembly (IL call-site count, not just source text), when the constructor no longer registers before the slow init steps, or when the match-start auto-on decision core cannot engage from the loading-screen conditions the shipped bug produced.

v0.1.2.32 (2026-11-21) [testing]
- Fixed: rotations never loaded, so the plugin did nothing in PvP matches since v0.1.2.26. The duty-rotation engine removal (v0.1.2.23) had also removed the single call in Updaters/RotationUpdater.cs LoadBuiltInRotations that fills CustomRotations from the assembly scan (LoadCustomRotationGroup); the rotation list stayed empty, the log stopped right after "MajorUpdater: triggering rotation load..." and no rotation was ever selected, with no error line anywhere.
- Restored that call and the "LoadBuiltInRotations: found N rotation groups" log line; a scan that finds no rotation groups now logs an error instead of staying silent (Updaters/RotationUpdater.cs, LoadBuiltInRotations).
- Added a release-harness gate (tests/PvPSolver.RotationHarness, RotationLoaderWiring) that fails when the rotation-load wiring is severed or the shipped assembly contains no loadable rotation - the regression class that passed every existing gate in v0.1.2.26 - v0.1.2.31.
- No PvE rotation content or behaviour returns; the PvP-only scope is unchanged. Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.31 (2026-11-20) [testing]
- Round 6 completion: the post-release marker grep still found four generated StatusID entries whose description text carries a marker word (ThrownForALoop, Soteria, BackFromTheBrink, BannerOfHonedAcuity). All four are unreferenced PvE statuses and are removed from the generated table; no code reads them.
- No code change and no PvP behaviour change; every remaining marker hit is a cited part of a PvP path (the Sage Kardia and Dancer partner targeting, and the tank lock-on VFX check).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.

e8f691d: Merge pull request #816 from SlashNephy/feat/alic-hunt-journeys

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
97ddbb9: Merge pull request #815 from SlashNephy/fix/alic-detect-world

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon
e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

DetectWorld picked the first public world in World sheet order whose
name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link
trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

- Prefer the world name right after the cross world icon, or the cross
  world character typed as text
- Otherwise use the world name that appears last in the message

Close #661

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying
7900863: fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying

Faloop responds to a login with wrong credentials with 400 and
{"success":false,"msg":"Incorrect username or password."}. The client
threw on it, so nothing was shown in chat, and the connection loop
treated it as a transient error and kept retrying.

- Read the 400 response as a rejected login instead of throwing
- Print the reason to chat and stop retrying

33272b7: feat(FaloopIntegration): notify when a scheduled spawn is released

Scheduled spawns are visible only to early access reporters at first,
and released to everyone later. The spawn_release handler was removed in
ac3fe87, so the release was no longer notified.

- Mark the spawn report of a scheduled spawn with "(scheduled)"
- Add a per-rank "Enable Mob Release Report" option (disabled by
  default) to notify "has been released!" on spawn_release
- Keep the stored spawn up to date on spawn_release even when the
  option is disabled
- Accept ISO 8601 strings as well as epoch milliseconds for the release
  timestamp, as Faloop's web client does

Close #685

3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit

  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection
47500d7: fix(FaloopIntegration): log the whole spawn_location payload

Passing the nullable ZonePoiId alone as the params argument of the log
call made it a null array when the value was null (CS8604). Log the
whole payload instead, as the spawn case does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while

trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
97ddbb9: Merge pull request #815 from SlashNephy/fix/alic-detect-world

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon
e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

DetectWorld picked the first public world in World sheet order whose
name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link
trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

- Prefer the world name right after the cross world icon, or the cross
  world character typed as text
- Otherwise use the world name that appears last in the message

Close #661

7900863: fix(FaloopIntegration): report rejected logins instead of retrying

Faloop responds to a login with wrong credentials with 400 and
{"success":false,"msg":"Incorrect username or password."}. The client
threw on it, so nothing was shown in chat, and the connection loop
treated it as a transient error and kept retrying.

- Read the 400 response as a rejected login instead of throwing
- Print the reason to chat and stop retrying

3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.

Yanxia example in #656.

  map markers found no other missing exit

  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known

the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

47500d7: fix(FaloopIntegration): log the whole spawn_location payload

Passing the nullable ZonePoiId alone as the params argument of the log
call made it a null array when the value was null (CS8604). Log the
whole payload instead, as the spawn case does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

HQ-only sets are reported as \"the dresser will not take HQ gear as an outfit glamour\" instead of failing after a click. Slot diagnostics also show each planned piece's quality. v1.3.0.17: Failed outfit stores now report the game's own reason — chat messages printed during the attempt are logged under \"game said:\" and the result reads \"The game did not accept this outfit (left for manual review)\", so the remaining refusals can be identified exactly instead of guessed. v1.3.0.16: Confirmation now clicks the real Yes button first (what a player does), then falls back to callback event 2 and event 0 in stages — the seasonal dialog was closing without depositing when only callbacks were fired. Combined with 1.3.0.15, \"already in the stored outfit\" is reported as ALREADY and is no longer counted as a store. v1.3.0.15: Honest results — \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" is now its own ALREADY state and no longer counts as a successful store; the tally reads stored / already there / need attention / failed. The store step also logs the click and, if no confirmation opens within 2 s, fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) before giving up. v1.3.0.14: Diagnosis + fallback for the seasonal Outfit Glamour Creation stalls — the store step now logs the addon state, hand-in counts and every slot (item id, inventory type, flag), and if no confirmation opens within 2 s it fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) as a fallback. v1.3.0.13: Quality consistency for outfit hand-ins — the outfit window only accepts pieces of one quality (\"Only items of the same quality may be selected\") and a mixed HQ/NQ selection made the game silently refuse the store while leaving the window open. The plugin now anchors on the quality it holds most of and hands in only pieces of that quality, logging any piece skipped for quality. v1.3.0.12: Checkbox-dialog fix — the confirm ladder now ticks the \"Store as Outfit Glamour\" checkbox first (synthetic ButtonClick + SetChecked) and fires Yes once the game enables it, instead of firing the default-confirm callback first, which closed the dialog without depositing on several sets (the \"checkbox was never selected\" symptom). The default-confirm callback is kept as a fallback for dialogs whose Yes cannot be enabled from the checkbox. v1.3.0.11: Cross-set outfit mismatch guard — a glamour piece can belong to more than one outfit set, and the game may open a different set's stored outfit when completing; the plugin now compares the opened outfit's item id with the planned set and skips with \"left for manual review\" instead of handing the piece into the wrong outfit and reporting a false failure. The store log keeps the dialog mode and prism-box index so any remaining case is diagnosable. v1.3.0.10: Fix the \"No deposit detected\" failures on outfit completions. The hand-in loop was allowed to target a slot already marked Filled (the outfit already contained that piece), which the game silently refused; it now only hands into Unfilled slots, and a set whose planned pieces are all already inside the outfit reports \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" instead of attempting a store. The native StoreExistingOutfit retry from 1.3.0.9 is removed — it returns success but deposits nothing unless the Glamour Creation window drives it. v1.3.0.9: Fix false \"No deposit detected\" results when completing an outfit — the game's confirm dialog sometimes closes without depositing for outfits that were only just created. After 1.5 s without a change the plugin now sends the same request the dialog sends (StoreExistingOutfit/StoreNewOutfit) once, then re-checks; store logs also report the dialog mode and prism-box index for diagnosis. v1.3.0.8: Withdraw tab clarity — the action buttons now state what they will do and grey out with an explicit empty-state label: \"No duplicates to withdraw\", \"No singles to withdraw\", and \"No sets to withdraw & re-deposit\" when there is nothing to pack (otherwise \"Withdraw & re-deposit sets (N)\" with counts). The consolidation description now explains the withdraw-then-pack-as-outfit loop and the slot saving. v1.3.0.7: Fix a window render crash when the set-consolidation loop ran with no loose set pieces left to start (the empty candidate list was indexed directly) — it now reports \"Nothing to consolidate\" instead. The consolidation pump is also exception-guarded so a future error cannot take the whole window down. v1.3.0.6: Set consolidation now runs in bag-sized batches — it withdraws one set's loose pieces (only as many as your free bag slots can hold), stores that set as a single outfit glamour, then repeats automatically. Before this the button tried to withdraw every loose set piece at once (359 items against 63 free slots) and was refused. v1.3.0.5: Dresser-full handling — at 800/800 the store run now stops with a clear 'Glamour Dresser is full' result instead of failing every remaining item with 'no deposit detected'. New \"set pieces stored loose\" detector on the Withdraw tab: it finds items the dresser stores individually that belong to an outfit set, shows how many pieces/sets and the approximate slots that would be freed, withdraws them (arm-then-confirm), then automatically runs the store pass that packs each set into one outfit glamour. v1.3.0.4: Single-item deposits now work — loose glamour items (not part of an outfit set) are stored with the game's own prism-box request command (the same request the Glamour Creation window's Yes button sends) instead of trying to open the outfit-store window, which the game only opens for set items. Each item costs one glamour prism (checked first) and the result reports \"Stored item (dresser X->Y)\". Outfit sets keep the existing flow. v1.3.0.3: Withdraw fix — the extractor was waiting on the dresser's 'requested' flag, which stays set while the data is loaded, so a run could stop before sending anything (\"the dresser data stayed busy\"); it now only gates on the loaded flag and retries refused sends. Store: the hand-in window is allowed to finish populating before the fill step decides nothing can be handed over. UI: two pages — Deposit (scan/store) and Withdraw (extractor) — with Abort reachable on the active page. v1.3.0.2: Gear-set protection hardening — items saved in a gear set are now detected from the saved gearset entries as well as the game's gear-set icon check (a 1.3.0.0 test scan saw 110 protected pieces on one pass and only 1 on another, so a piece could be misfiled as sortable). Deposit verification now reads the dresser list from MirageManager, so a dresser window that is momentarily unreadable no longer turns a successful deposit into a false \"couldn't read the dresser\" warning. v1.3.0.1: Fixes from the first 1.3.0.0 test. The dresser's \"Add to pre-existing outfit glamour?\" Yes/No prompt (shown when completing a stored outfit) is now answered automatically — before this it left the store flow stuck with the prompt on screen and froze the run. The Abort button stays clickable while a run is in progress. New watchdogs stop a set whose store window never opens or never produces its confirmation instead of stalling the rest of the run. Extractor: a refused RestorePrismBoxItem is retried (the client briefly refuses while a previous restore settles), waits for the dresser data request to finish, and skips further copies of a unique item (the game cannot give you a second copy while you hold one) instead of stopping the whole run; log lines now name the refused item. v1.3.0.0: Loose items — glamour-able items that belong to no outfit set are now stored as well, one at a time, and skipped when that item is already anywhere in the dresser. Extractor — withdraw dresser items back into your bags: all loose items, duplicates only (keeps one of each), or one item or item type such as all rings, with a live progress line. Item names and icons — planned pieces, duplicates and results now show the item icon, name and category instead of a raw item id. v1.2.0.1: Audit fixes. Completing an existing outfit works again — the pieces a stored outfit is still missing are planned as needed and are no longer listed as sellable duplicates. Deposit verification also accepts the planned pieces leaving your bags, so completing an outfit (or storing with a nearly full dresser) reports correctly instead of \"No deposit detected\". Store steps can no longer drop a set silently when a window does not open or the dresser closes mid-run, the store loop retries briefly while the dresser data reloads instead of stopping the rest of the run, and the Armoire toggle is locked while storing. /xllog now logs the scanned dresser/held counts for troubleshooting. v1.2.0.0: Full audit. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. The dresser's expanded item list is scanned, and a never-fill guard skips window slots the game already marks as part of the stored outfit. New model-duplicate hints show when a planned piece shares its appearance with something already stored. Deposit verification now retries briefly instead of failing on a single read. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections. Removed diagnostic logging. v1.1.1.0: The Store as Outfit Glamour checkbox dialog is now automated (synthetic checkbox click + default-confirm callback); all sets route to the dresser. v1.1.0.0: Armoire routing added.","IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"_SourceId":"dexcss-dalamudplugins","_SourceName":"dexcss / DalamudPlugins","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json","_Category":"qol"}
